From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@hortonhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Quick pulse: 60-second review + gift card fulfillment

Hi Taylor —

Thanks again for running the pilot with Redwood Inference this quarter. The team was great to work with and we appreciated the open feedback; the pilot summary is attached for your records.

If Horton Health had a moment, would you be willing to leave a very short public review (G2 or Capterra) about the deployment experience? We’re aiming for a one-paragraph, 60-second note — something like what you liked and any measurable wins (latency improvements, cost reduction, fewer infra headaches).

To make it easy, here are the links (choose whichever you prefer):
- G2: https://app.g2.com/reviews/new?product_id=redwood-inference
- Capterra: https://www.capterra.com/reviews/submit

As a small thank you, we offer a $75 Amazon e-gift card after the review is published. If you prefer a different vendor or need corporate coordination, please tell us how to route the fulfillment.

Next steps we suggest:
- If you can post something by end of next week, reply here and we’ll confirm the reward and registry details.
- If procurement needs documentation, Marcus can loop in any artifact or PO.

Appreciate it — no pressure at all. A short public note helps other healthcare teams evaluate real-world performance and makes a big difference for us.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Customer Advocacy | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com]
[Attachment: pilot-summary.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)]

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor@hortonhealth.com>

Subject: Re: Quick pulse: 60-second review + gift card fulfillment

Hi Jasmine —

Thanks for the note and the summary — looks good. A couple quick questions before we post:  
1) Will the review display any customer data or quotes pulled from our pilot artifacts? We need to ensure nothing PHI-related or proprietary appears.
2) Can the review be posted anonymously or with just the company name (Horton Health) and role? Our communications team is cautious about staff names.
3) For the gift card: procurement prefers corporate handling. Can you send an invoice or a vendor form, or is it easier to issue the e-gift card to my work email for internal distribution?

If anonymous posting is fine and there is no PHI, I'm happy to submit a short note about latency improvements and ease of rollout.

Thanks —
Taylor Nguyen
Director, Infrastructure & Cloud Services
Horton Health
(taylor@hortonhealth.com)

Hi Taylor —

Great questions — short answers below and happy to adjust to your orgs' process.

1) Privacy: The review form only contains free-text fields (no attachments) and we do not publish any pilot artifacts. If you avoid quoting logs or configs with PHI, nothing in the review will expose protected data. We can also request that the review be posted with a company name only; the public listing will show Horton Health but we will not include any internal documents.

2) Anonymity: You can absolutely post without personal names — just "Horton Health, Director of Infrastructure" or similar. If you'd prefer me to draft a 1–2 sentence suggestion for you to copy/paste, I can do that.

3) Gift card fulfillment: Monica is CC'd and will handle the e-gift form. If procurement requires an invoice or a vendor form, Marcus can produce a short receipt and compliance blurb. Otherwise, we can send the Amazon e-gift card to your work email and you can route it internally.

Monica — can you confirm the fulfillment flow (email vs procurement pop)? Also attaching the pilot summary again.

Thanks —
Jasmine
Customer Advocacy | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwood.inference.com]
[Attachment: pilot-summary.pdf (PDF, 420 KB)]

Happy to handle this. Options we can support:  
A) Send $75 Amazon e-gift card to your work email (fast, no procurement paperwork).
B) If procurement requires a corporate vendor payment, we can issue a small vendor credit; that will need a short PO (we can accept a scanned PO + vendor form).

Please reply with your preference. If option A, confirm the email to send the e-gift to and I’ll process it within 24 business hours of the review being live.

For your convenience we also have a short suggested blurb you can paste into G2:  
"Horton Health reduced inference latency by ~35% after switching to Redwood Inference. Deployment was straightforward and the team responded quickly to questions."

If you want this anonymized further, let me know and I’ll shorten it.
